description: Under a crust of cooled rock, a fistful of heat going out. To strike, it splits along the seams and flares.
lore: There is a stretch of the mountain that is the wrong colour and warm through the boot. No account of why has ever satisfied anybody, and the disagreement is half of what keeps the place going: argued over, walked around, described in detail to people who have never been within a day of it, and hardly ever crossed. Things get up out of ground held that way.

This one is mostly crust. Everybody who ever sat close to a fire remembers the same thing about one, and it is not the flame — it is the black skin that forms over a log late in the evening with the red still moving underneath. Everyone has that part exactly, so that is the part that stood up: a fistful of banked heat in a shell of cooled rock, going out from the moment it got up.

It fights by splitting. The shell opens along its seams, the heat comes out all at once and very bright, and then the shell shuts and there is a little less inside than there was. It cannot do that many times. Nothing about the arrangement suggests it was built to last, and nothing about it suggests it minds.

Coming apart, the light goes first. The yellow drains back out of the seams, the red follows it, and the shell crumbles smaller and smaller until there is not enough left of it to crumble. What is on the ground afterwards is the litter a fire leaves: a faceted lump of orange stone still lit along its splits, a piece or two of black glass keen enough to shave with, and one ember down in the middle of it that will not go out however long you wait.

The ember is the hard piece — scorched dark red, more embers sulking in its cracks, warm in the pocket and warm a hundred years from now. It does not burn hot in a blade. It warms one, and it warms whoever is carrying it, and it takes the worst out of a fire that would otherwise have had the skin off them. Which is right, because what it is the last of was never the burning. It is being warm.
